blocks.prompt: 10. [printed as 9.] Find the area of the region bounded by the line \(y = x + 1\) and the parabola \(y^{2} = 2x + 10\).
blocks.explanation:
Parabola \(y^{2} = 2x + 10\) left-right khulta hai (letta hua).
Agar vertical strips lein to bayen hisse mein strip parabola se parabola tak jati hai aur dayen hisse mein parabola se line tak, yani do alag formulas aur do integrals.
Horizontal strips lena kahin aasaan hai: dono curves ko \(x\) in terms of \(y\) likh kar \(A = \int_c^d (x_{\text{right}} - x_{\text{left}})\,dy\).
Plan: \(x\) ko \(y\) mein likhna, milne ke points, dayen kaun, integral.
steps:
Diya gaya: line \(y = x + 1\) aur parabola \(y^{2} = 2x + 10\).
Maloom karna: band area.
Tareeqa: \(y\) ke lehaaz se integral: (dayen wali curve) minus (bayen wali curve).

Qadam 1: \(x\) ko \(y\) mein likhein
\[\text{line: } x = y - 1\]
\[\text{parabola: } x = \dfrac{y^{2} - 10}{2}\]
Kyun: Horizontal strip bayen curve se dayen curve tak jati hai, is liye dono ka \(x\) chahiye. Parabola se \(2x = y^{2} - 10\), phir 2 se divide.

Qadam 2: Intersection points
\[y - 1 = \dfrac{y^{2} - 10}{2} \Rightarrow y^{2} - 2y - 8 = 0\]
\[(y - 4)(y + 2) = 0 \Rightarrow y = 4,\ -2\]
Points: \((3, 4)\) aur \((-3, -2)\).
Kyun: Dono \(x\) barabar rakhe, 2 se multiply kiya: \(2y - 2 = y^{2} - 10\). Yeh \(y\)-values hi limits hain; \(x\) line se mila: \(x = y - 1\).

Qadam 3: Dayen kaun hai?
\(y = 0\) par: line \(x = -1\), parabola \(x = -5\). Line dayen taraf hai.
Kyun: Integrand dayen minus bayen hona chahiye taake positive aaye; jis ka \(x\) bara woh dayen hai.
Dhyan dein: Yahan "upar/neeche" nahi, "dayen/bayen" sochna hai. Ulta le liya to jawab \(-18\) aayega.

Qadam 4: Integrate karein
\[A = \int_{-2}^{4}\left[(y - 1) - \dfrac{y^{2} - 10}{2}\right]dy\]
\[= \int_{-2}^{4}\left(-\dfrac{y^{2}}{2} + y + 4\right)dy\]
\[= \left[-\dfrac{y^{3}}{6} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{2} + 4y\right]_{-2}^{4}\]
\[= \dfrac{40}{3} - \left(-\dfrac{14}{3}\right) = 18\]
Kyun: Bracket khol kar \(-1 + 5 = 4\) mila. \(y = 4\) par: \(-\frac{64}{6} + 8 + 16 = \frac{40}{3}\); \(y = -2\) par: \(\frac{8}{6} + 2 - 8 = -\frac{14}{3}\). Minus ka minus plus ban gaya: \(\frac{54}{3} = 18\).

Tasdeeq:
Parabola \(x = \frac{1}{2}y^{2} + \dots\) aur us ki chord jo \(y = \alpha, \beta\) par mile, un ke darmiyan area \(\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{(\beta - \alpha)^{3}}{6}\) hota hai. Yahan \(\beta - \alpha = 6\): \(\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{216}{6} = 18\). Jawab mil gaya.
